title: Jamming states in random sequential adsorption of diffusion-limited aggregates
authors: Fahad Puthalath, Dipanjan Mandal, Sumanta Kundu
abstract: Motivated by the ubiquity of ramified fractal deposits in nature and engineered systems, we investigate the irreversible adsorption of diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) clusters on a square lattice. We study the role of cluster shape diversity on jamming properties of the system by systematically controlling the number of distinct shapes used across and within realizations, encompassing both monodisperse and polydisperse model variants. Our large-scale simulations over a broad range of cluster sizes $2\leqslant k\leqslant4096$ show that the jamming density decreases with cluster size as a power-law $p_j(k)-p_j^\infty\sim k^{-α}$. Both $α$ and $p_j^\infty$ are found to depend on the degree of shape diversity, with $α$ ranging from $0.374(2)$ to $0.417(1)$. It is observed that increasing shape polydispersity promotes denser packing. Importantly, the fluctuations of the jamming density exhibit distinct scaling behavior: $σ(L)\sim1/L$ for a fixed pool of cluster shape(s), but remain $L$-independent when the pool of shape(s) is refreshed across different realizations. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the differences between the model variants systematically diminish with increasing $k$ and are expected to vanish as $k\to\infty$ due to the statistical self-similarity of the DLA clusters.
summary: This paper simulates the random sequential adsorption of DLA clusters on a lattice to study jamming states. It systematically analyzes how varying the diversity of cluster shapes—from fixed to highly polydisperse—affects the final jamming density and its fluctuations. The findings reveal that increased shape diversity leads to denser packing, providing quantitative scaling laws for these non-equilibrium deposition processes.
main_problem: The study investigates how the diversity of cluster shapes affects the jamming properties when using Diffusion-Limited Aggregation (DLA) clusters for irreversible adsorption.
main_result: The jamming density decreases with cluster size as a power-law, and increasing shape polydispersity promotes denser packing. Furthermore, the fluctuation scaling of the jamming density differs significantly depending on whether the cluster shape pool is fixed or refreshed.
method: The research employs large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to model the Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) process using DLA clusters on a square lattice.
model_or_system: The system is the irreversible adsorption of DLA clusters on a square lattice, analyzed through several model variants: fixed-shape, refreshing-shape, and polydisperse variants controlled by a pool size $S$.
key_observables: Jamming density ($p_j$), the scaling exponent $\alpha$ in $p_j(k) - p_\infty \sim k^{-\alpha}$, and the fluctuation of the jamming density ($\sigma(L)$).
important_parameters: Cluster size ($k$), system size ($L$), and the degree of shape diversity (controlled by $S$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that differences between model variants diminish at very large cluster sizes ($k 	o \infty$) due to the statistical self-similarity of DLA clusters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative DLA clusters showing shape diversity and show the scaling behavior of the jamming density and its fluctuations ($\sigma(L)$) for different model variants.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares results from multiple model variants (fixed vs. refreshing vs. polydisperse) to quantify the role of shape diversity on the jamming density and its fluctuations, establishing scaling laws for both observables.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the study of jamming transitions and the role of quenched disorder (shape diversity) in determining macroscopic properties has analogies in understanding complex energy landscapes or disordered quantum systems.
